  3. Artistic new tab

#Artistic new tab

When browser.newtab.art.enabled is on, a new tab shows a random public-domain painting filling the window, with the start page's shortcuts and the address bar legible over it, a discreet caption (title, artist, date, museum, a link to the record) and two small buttons (Another painting, Open the record). It follows Google Arts & Culture's "art new tab" idea, but every piece runs natively in Wren: the engine renders the page, the shell downloads and caches the images. The option is off by default.

#When the network is touched

Never while the option is off, and never while the loader is held offline. With the option on, the paintings an earlier session kept and nobody saw yet are taken back at the start, without the network, so the first new tab has one at once. A background task then starts about 2.5 seconds after the start (or after the option is turned on), so that a first session has one too; it also starts at the first art new tab if it was stopped. Until a painting is ready, the new tab shows a gradient with a spinner and "Fetching a painting…", and is replaced by the painting as soon as one is. From then on the task keeps a sliding window of about browser.newtab.art.window paintings ready, downloading a fresh one whenever a shown painting is consumed. The task stops after browser.newtab.art.idle_minutes with no art new tab shown and resumes at the next one.

The only requests made are the source's listing API and the image files themselves. Nothing about the user is sent: no identifier, no third-party referrer, an honest User-Agent (Wren/<version>). The images and their metadata live only in the profile's temporary folder (<profile>/tmp/newtab-art), one JSON file of metadata beside each image, and are removed with Clear browsing data (the "cached responses" kind, for all sites).

#Sources

browser.newtab.art.sources is a comma list tried in turn (replaceable):

  • cleveland — Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access. CC0 paintings, no key. A random slice of the ~3,900 CC0 paintings is listed; the larger images.print rendition is used, falling back to images.web (~900 px).
  • commons — Wikimedia Commons. The Google Art Project works by artist and Featured pictures of paintings categories, listed with generator=categorymembers and prop=imageinfo (iiurlwidth for a bounded width, extmetadata for artist, title and licence). Only freely licensed files are kept (public domain, CC0, CC-BY / CC-BY-SA); non-commercial, no-derivatives and fair-use files are refused. The attribution is shown in the caption.

Google Arts & Culture itself has no public API and is not used. The Met (search returns 410) and the Art Institute of Chicago (Cloudflare challenge) do not answer a client without a browser reliably and are not used either.

#Courtesy and validation

The downloader makes one request at a time per host and backs off exponentially on 429 / 403 / network error (browser.newtab.art.backoff_base_ms doubling up to browser.newtab.art.backoff_max_ms). Every answer is validated before it is kept: an image/* MIME type, a size below browser.newtab.art.max_image_bytes, a known image signature, a decode with Wren's own image decoder, a sane aspect ratio (between 1:3 and 3:1) and a minimum width (browser.newtab.art.min_width_px, 1280 px by default, of the file as it came) for full-screen use.

#What is kept, and what a new tab costs

Museums serve paintings for print: 4 MB on average, up to 8 MB and 3400 px. A new tab needs a screenful, so the work is done once, when a painting arrives and in the background: the decoder reduces it to browser.newtab.art.short_side_px on its shorter side (the side that matters for an image that covers a window), and a worker encodes that as JPEG (browser.newtab.art.jpeg_quality) and writes it with its JSON file. A file that needed no reducing and is at most 1 MB is kept as it came, and so is one whose JPEG would be no smaller.

The page is a few kilobytes and names the file at a file: address: the page's loader reads it off the window's thread and the decoder decodes it at the size it is kept at. The page may read that folder and nothing else; with security.file_access.policy=none it reads nothing and shows its gradient.

Measured on the development machine (2026-11-04, a window of 1920 x 1080, headless, from the navigation to the painting in a frame; the longest wait for a frame in brackets):

What the new tab loadsBefore: a data: URLA file: addressKept as it is now
A painting of 8 MB, 2833 x 3400950 ms (770 ms)165 ms (25 ms)40 ms (15 ms), 0.6 MB
A painting of 4.4 MB640 ms (450 ms)40 ms (14 ms), 0.3 MB

The disk holds what was not seen yet. A shown painting leaves it two picks later (its tab has read it by then), and the first look at the folder in a session keeps the newest browser.newtab.art.window paintings within browser.newtab.art.max_cache_mb and removes everything else: other formats, strays, what a crash left. While the task runs, files beyond browser.newtab.art.max_cache_mb are purged oldest first.

#"Smart"

The painting chosen for a new tab suits the window's orientation (landscape for a wide window, portrait for a tall one); a painting of the other orientation is shown whole over a blurred fill of itself rather than cropped to a sliver. The last browser.newtab.art.window picks are remembered so the same painting does not repeat at once, and the next one is pre-fetched while the current is on screen. Nothing downloads on a limited or offline connection.

#Preferences

PreferenceDefaultWhat it does
browser.newtab.art.enabledfalseTurn the artistic new tab on.
browser.newtab.art.sourcescleveland,commonsWhere paintings come from, a comma list.
browser.newtab.art.window20How many paintings are kept ready (the sliding window).
browser.newtab.art.max_cache_mb128Most disk the cached paintings take.
browser.newtab.art.refresh_hours12A kept painting older than this is refreshed. 0 = never.
browser.newtab.art.show_captiontrueShow the caption at the bottom.
browser.newtab.art.offline_fallbacktrueAn elegant gradient with the caption when nothing is ready yet.
browser.newtab.art.min_width_px1280Smallest width a painting may have.
browser.newtab.art.max_image_bytes8 MBLargest image file downloaded.
browser.newtab.art.short_side_px1600A painting is kept with its shorter side at most this long.
browser.newtab.art.jpeg_quality0.82Quality of the JPEG a reduced painting is kept as.
browser.newtab.art.idle_minutes30Stop the task after this long with no art new tab. 0 = never.
browser.newtab.art.backoff_base_ms2000First retry wait after a failure (doubles).
browser.newtab.art.backoff_max_ms300000Longest retry wait.

#Trying it

  1. Open about:config, set browser.newtab.art.enabled to true.
  2. Open a new tab (Ctrl+T). The first one may be the plain start page or the fallback gradient while the first paintings download; open a few more tabs and they fill with paintings.
  3. Another painting (or opening about:home?art=next) shows the next one; Open the record opens the museum's page for the painting.
  4. Clear browsing data (about:sites, "cached responses" for all sites) empties the cache; the task refills it.
